lines.text: In seventy-nine AD, Mount Vesuvius unleashed a fury one hundred thousand times greater than an atomic blast.
For hours, Pompeii was buried beneath falling pumice stone, turning mid-day into pitch-black night.
Then, at dawn, a superheated pyroclastic avalanche roared down the mountain at hurricane speed, freezing an entire city at five hundred degrees.
Under meters of hardened volcanic debris, Pompeii remained silent and forgotten for nearly two thousand years.
Centuries later, archaeologists poured plaster into hollow voids in the ash, revealing the harrowing final moments of Roman citizens frozen mid-breath.
A bustling metropolis vanished in hours, perfectly preserved in eternal stone. Subscribe to Beyond History for more.
